---
title: nexum-xilem Reference
description: Xilem adapter — setup, the with_deep_links view wrapper and message-relay behavior.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`nexum-xilem` routes deep-link events into Xilem's view tree through a task-based relay. It re-exports the core types and the `platform` module alias like every adapter.

## API

| Item | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup` | `fn setup(config: &Config) -> Result<()>` | Registers with the OS and stores the handle process-globally; `HubAlreadySet` on double init |
| `handle` | `fn handle() -> &'static DeepLinkHandle` | The stored handle; **panics** if `setup` was not called |
| `with_deep_links` | `fn with_deep_links<State, V>(view: V, on_url: impl Fn(&mut State, String) + Send + Sync + 'static) -> impl WidgetView<State>` | Wraps a view: forks a Xilem task that forwards URLs to `on_url` |

`State` must be `'static` and `V` a `WidgetView<State>`. No feature flags exist — everything is always available.

## Usage

<Code lang="rust" code={`nexum_xilem::setup(&config).expect("deep-link setup");

fn app_logic(state: &mut AppState) -> impl WidgetView<AppState> + use<> {
    let content = /* your normal view */;
    with_deep_links(content, |state: &mut AppState, url| {
                    state.last_url = Some(url);
    })
}`} />

## How delivery works

`with_deep_links` builds a `task_raw` whose async body awaits `handle.recv()` in a loop and pushes each URL through Xilem's `MessageProxy`; the returned task is combined with your view via `fork`. Consequences worth knowing:

- The `on_url` callback runs on the **app thread**, exactly like a regular Xilem event callback — no extra synchronization needed for `State`.
- The relay ends silently when the view tree or driver goes away (the proxy reports a send error), so teardown is automatic.
- Calling `handle()` or `with_deep_links` before `setup` panics with `nexum_xilem::setup must be called before consuming deep links` — a deliberate programming-error signal.

<Aside type="tip">
Because `setup` is fallible and `with_deep_links` is not, call `setup` in `main` before constructing the `Xilem` driver, then treat the rest of the integration as infallible.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Async consumption guide" href="/guides/async-consumption/" description="The recv loop this adapter runs on your behalf." />
- <LinkCard title="Core reference" href="/reference/core/" description="The handle stored by setup." />


---

---
title: nexum-core Reference
description: Config, ConfigBuilder, AppLink, DeepLinkHub, DeepLinkHandle, DeepLinkEvent, Source and DeepLinkStream — the framework-independent primitives.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`nexum-core` holds everything that does not touch the operating system: configuration, the producer-consumer event channel, and the event type. All items are re-exported flat from the crate root, and the crate compiles with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. The transport is `async-channel`, so every async API works on any executor — and on wasm.

## Config

Describes what your application owns and how it presents itself to the OS.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemes` | `Vec<String>` | `[]` | URL schemes the app handles, e.g. `myapp` |
| `app_links` | `Vec<AppLink>` | `[]` | App links (universal links) the app claims |
| `icon_path` | `Option<PathBuf>` | `None` | Icon for the OS protocol handler (Windows `DefaultIcon`, Linux `Icon=`) |

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new` | `fn new(schemes: impl IntoIterator<Item: Into<String>>) -> Self` | Struct-literal-friendly constructor from schemes |
| `builder` | `fn builder() -> ConfigBuilder` | Returns a fresh builder |
| `with_app_links` | `fn with_app_links(self, links: impl IntoIterator<Item = AppLink>) -> Self` | **Replaces** the app-link list |
| `with_app_link` | `fn with_app_link(self, link: AppLink) -> Self` | Appends one app link |
| `with_icon_path` | `fn with_icon_path(self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self` | Sets the icon path |
| `validate` | `fn validate(&self) -> Result<()>` | Checks schemes against the RFC 3986 grammar and app-link hosts |
| `validate_scheme` | `fn validate_scheme(scheme: &str) -> Result<()>` | Associated function: first char ASCII alphabetic, then alphanumerics or `+ - .` |
| `extract_launch_urls` | `fn extract_launch_urls<I>(&self, args: I) -> Vec<String>` | Keeps every argument that parses as an absolute URL with a configured scheme (case-insensitive); preserves order; accepts scheme-only URLs like `myapp:` |

## ConfigBuilder

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scheme` | `fn scheme(self, scheme: impl Into<String>) -> Self` | Appends one scheme |
| `schemes` | `fn schemes(self, schemes: impl IntoIterator<Item: Into<String>>) -> Self` | Appends several |
| `app_link` | `fn app_link(self, link: AppLink) -> Self` | Appends one app link |
| `app_links` | `fn app_links(self, links: impl IntoIterator<Item = AppLink>) -> Self` | Appends several |
| `icon_path` | `fn icon_path(self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self` | Sets the icon path |
| `build` | `fn build(self) -> Result<Config>` | Builds and runs `validate`; an empty builder fails with `Error::NoSchemes` |

## AppLink

| Field / method | Type or signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `String` | The host this app claims, e.g. `example.com` |
| `path_prefixes` | `Vec<String>` | Each starts with `/`; an empty list claims the whole host |
| `new` | `fn new(host: impl Into<String>, path_prefixes: impl IntoIterator<Item: Into<String>>) -> Self` | Constructor |

## DeepLinkHub — the producer

The hub owns the event queue. It is a multi-producer, **multi-consumer** channel: each event goes to exactly one consumer, chosen round-robin among live receivers. Clone handles for load-sharing; there is no broadcast.

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new` | `fn new() -> Self` | Unbounded queue (also `Default`) |
| `bounded` | `fn bounded(capacity: usize) -> Self` | Capacity clamped to at least 1; see the [bounded guide](/guides/bounded-hub/) |
| `capacity` | `fn capacity(&self) -> Option<usize>` | `None` means unbounded |
| `sender` | `fn sender(&self) -> async_channel::Sender<DeepLinkEvent>` | Escape hatch for custom framework bridges |
| `push_url` | `fn push_url(&self, url: impl Into<String>)` | Pushes with `Source::System`; blocks when a bounded queue is full; silently drops after shutdown |
| `push_launch_url` | `fn push_launch_url(&self, url: impl Into<String>)` | Pushes with `Source::CommandLine` |
| `try_push_url` | `fn try_push_url(&self, url: impl Into<String>) -> Result<(), Error>` | Non-blocking; `QueueFull` or `HubClosed` |
| `try_push_launch_url` | `fn try_push_launch_url(&self, url: impl Into<String>) -> Result<(), Error>` | Same, with `Source::CommandLine` |
| `push_event` | `fn push_event(&self, event: DeepLinkEvent)` | Pushes a pre-built event, keeping its source |
| `try_push_event` | `fn try_push_event(&self, event: DeepLinkEvent) -> Result<(), Error>` | Non-blocking variant |
| `handle` | `fn handle(&self) -> DeepLinkHandle` | Creates an additional consumer |

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum_core::{Config, DeepLinkHub, Source};

let config = Config::new(["myapp"]).validate().expect("valid config");
let hub = DeepLinkHub::new();
let handle = hub.handle();

hub.push_url("myapp://open/settings");
assert_eq!(handle.try_recv().as_deref(), Some("myapp://open/settings"));

hub.push_launch_url("myapp://open/doc/42");
let event = handle.recv_event_blocking().expect("event");
assert_eq!(event.source, Source::CommandLine);`} />

## DeepLinkHandle — the consumer

`DeepLinkHandle` is `Clone`; each clone is an independent consumer in the round-robin. Blocking methods are unavailable on wasm targets.

| Method | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new` | `fn new(rx: Receiver<DeepLinkEvent>) -> Self` | Adopts any raw `async_channel` receiver |
| `recv` | `async fn recv(&self) -> Option<String>` | `None` after shutdown |
| `recv_event` | `async fn recv_event(&self) -> Option<DeepLinkEvent>` | Async variant with source |
| `recv_url` | `async fn recv_url(&self) -> Option<Result<url::Url>>` | Malformed URL arrives as `Some(Err(_))` |
| `recv_blocking` | `fn recv_blocking(&self) -> Result<String>` | Native only; `Error::HubClosed` on shutdown |
| `recv_event_blocking` | `fn recv_event_blocking(&self) -> Result<DeepLinkEvent>` | Native only |
| `try_recv` | `fn try_recv(&self) -> Option<String>` | `None` when empty *or* closed (indistinguishable) |
| `try_recv_event` | `fn try_recv_event(&self) -> Option<DeepLinkEvent>` | Same semantics |
| `drain` | `fn drain(&self) -> Vec<String>` | All currently queued URLs, in order |
| `drain_events` | `fn drain_events(&self) -> Vec<DeepLinkEvent>` | Same for full events |
| `into_stream` | `fn into_stream(self) -> DeepLinkStream` | Requires the `stream` feature |

## DeepLinkEvent and Source

| Field / method | Type or signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `String` | The raw URL string as received |
| `source` | `Source` | Where the event came from |
| `new` | `fn new(url: impl Into<String>, source: Source) -> Self` | Constructor |
| `parse_url` | `fn parse_url(&self) -> Result<url::Url>` | Lazy parse; `Error::MalformedUrl` on failure |

| `Source` variant | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `System` *(default)* | Delivered by the OS while already running — registry hand-off (Windows), Apple event (macOS), forwarded hand-off, mobile intake |
| `CommandLine` | Found on this process's command line — cold start on Windows and Linux, macOS `GURL` events (see [event sources](/explanation/event-sources/)) |

## DeepLinkStream

With the `stream` feature, `into_stream` converts a handle into `DeepLinkStream`, which implements `futures_core::Stream` with `Item = String`. The stream terminates when the channel shuts down.

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Error reference" href="/reference/errors/" description="Every Error variant and when it surfaces." />
- <LinkCard title="Platform reference" href="/reference/platform/" description="OS registration and the global hub." />


---

---
title: Error Reference
description: Every variant of nexum_core::Error with its exact display message and the situations that produce it.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The whole nexum stack shares one error type: `nexum_core::Error`, built with `thiserror`. The type alias `Result<T, E = Error>` is re-exported alongside it, and `Error` is `Send + Sync + 'static` so it crosses threads and tasks freely.

| Variant | Display message | Produced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NoSchemes` | `at least one URL scheme must be configured` | `Config::validate` or `ConfigBuilder::build` with zero schemes |
| `InvalidScheme(String)` | `` `{0}` is not a valid URL scheme (RFC 3986: ALPHA *( ALPHA / DIGIT / "+" / "-" / "." )) `` | Scheme fails the RFC 3986 grammar check |
| `InvalidHost(String)` | `` `{0}` is not a valid app-link host `` | App link with an empty host |
| `HubAlreadySet` | `the deep-link hub is already initialized for this process` | `set_hub` or `init`/`init_with` called a second time (including adapters' internal setup) |
| `HubNotSet` | `no deep-link hub is initialized yet; call nexum_platform::init first` | Platform operation (`push_url`, `single_instance::acquire`, mobile intake) before initialization |
| `HubClosed` | `the deep-link channel has been shut down` | Blocking receive after every sender and receiver dropped |
| `QueueFull` | `the bounded deep-link queue is full` | `try_push_*` on a bounded hub at capacity |
| `MalformedUrl(String, url::ParseError)` | `` `{0}` is not a valid URL: {1} `` | Lazy parse failure via `DeepLinkEvent::parse_url` or `recv_url` items |
| `Platform(String)` | `platform registration failed: {0}` | Backend-specific failures: `xdg-mime` non-zero exit, main-thread violation on macOS, single-instance protocol errors |
| `Io(std::io::Error)` | *(transparent)* | Filesystem and socket I/O underneath registration |

## Matching examples

Error variants are plain enum variants, so `matches!` is the idiomatic guard:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum_core::{Config, Error};

let err = Config::builder().build().expect_err("no schemes");
assert!(matches!(err, Error::NoSchemes));

let err = Config::validate_scheme("1bad").expect_err("bad scheme");
assert!(matches!(err, Error::InvalidScheme(_)));`} />

## Recovery guidance

- `NoSchemes`, `InvalidScheme`, `InvalidHost` are configuration bugs — fail fast at startup.
- `HubAlreadySet` indicates double initialization; adapters surface the same variant when their own setup runs twice.
- `HubNotSet` means an ordering mistake: initialize the hub before any push, intake or `acquire` call.
- `HubClosed` and `QueueFull` are *flow control*, not faults: consumers stopped or backpressure engaged. Handle them in the retry/shutdown logic of your consumer loop.
- `Platform` wraps the largest class of environment problems — missing `xdg-mime`, a non-main-thread registration on macOS, or single-instance protocol mismatches. The inner string names the exact cause and is stable enough to log verbatim.

<Aside type="tip">
`Io` is transparent (`#[from]`), so `?` converts a `std::io::Error` into `Error` automatically in fallible glue code.
</Aside>

- <LinkCard title="Core reference" href="/reference/core/" description="Config and hub APIs that produce these errors." />
- <LinkCard title="Platform reference" href="/reference/platform/" description="Registration functions and their error behavior." />


---

---
title: The deep_link Attribute
description: Syntax, accepted keys, generated code and constraints of the nexum-macros bootstrap attribute.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`#[deep_link]` is the attribute macro exported by `nexum-macros` (and re-exported by the `nexum` facade). It rewrites a `fn main` so that deep-link registration happens **before** the first statement of the body executes, binding the consumer handle to a generated `_nexum_handle` binding.

## Syntax

| Key | Type | Required | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemes` | array of string literals, or a single string literal | **Yes** | One `Config::builder().scheme(...)` call per entry |
| `app_links` | array of string literals, or a single string literal | No | One `AppLink::new(host, [])` per entry (no path prefixes) |
| `icon` | single string literal | No | Passed to `.icon_path(...)` |

Unknown keys, bare values, or non-string values fail to compile with a targeted message — for example ``unknown key `foo`; expected `schemes`, `app_links` or `icon` ``.

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum::deep_link;

#[deep_link(schemes = ["myapp", "myapp-alt"], icon = "/icons/app.png")]
fn main() {
    if let Ok(url) = _nexum_handle.recv_blocking() {
                    println!("opened {url}");
    }
}`} />

## Generated code

The macro leaves your attributes, visibility and signature untouched and prepends one binding to the body:

<Code lang="rust" code={`let _nexum_handle = {
    let __nexum_config = ::nexum::Config::builder()
                    .scheme("myapp")
                    .build()
                    .expect("nexum: invalid deep-link configuration");
    ::nexum::platform::init(&__nexum_config)
                    .expect("nexum: deep-link initialization failed")
};
// ...your original statements...`} />

## Constraints

- **`fn main` only.** Applying the attribute to any other function is a compile error: `` `#[deep_link]` can only be applied to `fn main` ``.
- **Requires the facade.** The expansion references `::nexum::` absolute paths, so the macro only works when the `nexum` facade crate is a dependency — not with `nexum-macros` alone.
- **Panics on failure by design.** Invalid configuration and failed registration both panic with descriptive messages. If your app must recover — for example to show a dialog — call `nexum::platform::init` directly and handle the `Result` instead of using the attribute.
- **Registration timing.** Everything inside the generated block runs before your first statement, which also satisfies macOS's main-thread requirement for registration.

<Aside type="tip">
The generated `_nexum_handle` is a regular `DeepLinkHandle`: every consumption pattern from the [core reference](/reference/core/) — blocking, async, stream, bounded — applies unchanged.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Facade reference" href="/reference/nexum/" description="What the nexum crate re-exports alongside the macro." />
- <LinkCard title="Build your first deep link" href="/tutorials/getting-started/" description="The attribute in a complete, runnable walkthrough." />


---

---
title: nexum (Facade)
description: The one-dependency facade — re-exports of core primitives, the platform module and the deep_link bootstrap attribute.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The `nexum` crate is a convenience facade: it pulls together the three building blocks — core primitives, OS platform layer and the bootstrap macro — so a desktop application needs exactly one dependency. Everything on this page is a re-export; the detailed behavior lives in the linked component references.

## Re-exports

| Item | Source | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Config`, `ConfigBuilder`, `AppLink` | `nexum-core` | Declarative configuration of schemes, app links and icon |
| `DeepLinkHub` | `nexum-core` | Producer side of the event channel |
| `DeepLinkHandle` | `nexum-core` | Consumer side (blocking, async, polling, stream) |
| `DeepLinkEvent`, `Source` | `nexum-core` | The event payload and its origin |
| `Error`, `Result` | `nexum-core` | The shared error type |
| `DeepLinkStream` | `nexum-core` *(only with the `stream` feature)* | `Stream<Item = String>` over the handle |
| `deep_link` | `nexum-macros` | `#[deep_link(schemes = ["myapp"])]` bootstrap attribute |
| `platform` | `nexum-platform` | Whole module alias: `init`, `register`, `plist`, `mobile`, … |
| `hub`, `set_hub`, `push_url`, `push_launch_url`, `register`, `init`, `init_with` | `nexum-platform` | Flat re-exports of the root platform functions |
| `validate_bundle` | `nexum-platform` *(macOS targets only)* | Plist validator for the running app bundle |

## Feature flags

| Feature | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `stream` | Enables `nexum-core/stream` and re-exports `DeepLinkStream` |
| `single-instance` | Enables `nexum-platform/single-instance`, exposing `nexum::platform::single_instance` |

## Usage

The intended shape is one attribute on `main`:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum::deep_link;

#[deep_link(schemes = ["myapp"], icon = "/icons/app.png")]
fn main() {
    if let Ok(url) = _nexum_handle.recv_blocking() {
                    println!("opened {url}");
    }
}`} />

Prefer explicit control? The attribute is optional — `nexum::platform::init(&config)` returns the same `DeepLinkHandle` without any macro:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum::{Config, platform};

let config = Config::builder().scheme("myapp").build().expect("valid config");
let handle = platform::init(&config).expect("registration failed");`} />

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Core reference" href="/reference/core/" description="Config, DeepLinkHub, DeepLinkHandle, DeepLinkEvent signatures." />
- <LinkCard title="Platform reference" href="/reference/platform/" description="init, register, plist, mobile and single-instance APIs." />
- <LinkCard title="Macro reference" href="/reference/macros/" description="The #[deep_link] attribute syntax and expansion." />


---

---
title: nexum-platform Reference
description: OS registration, the process-global hub, plist validation, mobile intake and single-instance hand-off — signatures and platform behavior.
type: reference
---

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`nexum-platform` turns a `Config` into an OS-registered protocol handler and hosts the process-global hub that platform relays feed. Desktop backends are cfg-gated per target; `plist` and `mobile` compile everywhere; `single_instance` requires its feature flag on Unix or Windows.

## Root functions

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hub` | `fn hub() -> Option<&'static DeepLinkHub>` | The process-global hub, if initialized |
| `set_hub` | `fn set_hub(hub: DeepLinkHub) -> Result<()>` | Installs a custom global hub; `HubAlreadySet` on repeat calls |
| `push_url` | `fn push_url(url: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()>` | Pushes into the global hub with `Source::System`; `HubNotSet` before init |
| `push_launch_url` | `fn push_launch_url(url: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()>` | Same, with `Source::CommandLine` |
| `register` | `fn register(config: &Config) -> Result<()>` | Runs the platform backend, then relays cold-start URLs from `std::env::args().skip(1)`. On macOS it panics unless called from the main thread |
| `init` | `fn init(config: &Config) -> Result<DeepLinkHandle>` | `init_with(config, DeepLinkHub::new())` |
| `init_with` | `fn init_with(config: &Config, hub: DeepLinkHub) -> Result<DeepLinkHandle>` | Installs a specific hub (e.g. bounded) and registers; returns a handle to it |
| `validate_bundle` | `fn validate_bundle(config: &Config) -> Result<Vec<String>>` | macOS only (re-export from the backend): schemes missing from the running bundle's `Info.plist` |

`init` and `init_with` fail with `HubAlreadySet` when called twice — including indirectly, once an adapter has already initialized.

## Platform backends

| Backend | Registration writes | Runtime delivery | Cold start |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Per scheme under `HKCU\Software\Classes`: protocol marker, `DefaultIcon` (`icon_path` or exe), `shell\open\command` = `"{exe}" "%1"` | OS launches a second process; not a live event source | URL extracted from `argv`, pushed as `Source::CommandLine` |
| macOS | Nothing on disk — installs a `GURL` Apple-event delegate via `NSAppleEventManager` (main thread required) | Delegate pushes URLs into the hub via `push_launch_url` → `Source::CommandLine` | Same Apple-event path after delegate installation |
| Linux | `{data_local_dir}/applications/{app}.desktop` with `Exec`, `Icon`, `MimeType=x-scheme-handler/...`, then `xdg-mime default` per scheme | OS launches a second process | URL extracted from `argv`, pushed as `Source::CommandLine` |
| Android / iOS | Declarative generators (`mobile` + `plist` modules) | Framework glue calls the intake functions | Same intake path |

## plist module

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url_types_xml` | `fn url_types_xml(config: &Config) -> String` | Renders the full `CFBundleURLTypes` XML block for the configured schemes |
| `missing_schemes` | `fn missing_schemes(plist_xml: &str, config: &Config) -> Vec<String>` | Configured schemes absent from the given plist XML; case-insensitive; tolerant of arbitrary or broken formatting (a broken plist reports all schemes missing) |

## mobile module

| Function | Signature | Target | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `android_manifest_intent_filter` | `fn android_manifest_intent_filter(config: &Config) -> String` | All targets | Renders an `<intent-filter>` (VIEW, DEFAULT + BROWSABLE, one `<data>` per scheme) |
| `push_intent_url` | `fn push_intent_url(url: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()>` | `target_os = "android"` | Feeds `Intent.getDataString()` URLs from JNI glue into the hub as `Source::System` |
| `push_open_urls` | `fn push_open_urls<I>(urls: I) -> Result<()> where I: IntoIterator, I::Item: Into<String>` | `target_os = "ios"` | Feeds `openURLContexts`/`open URL:` delegate URLs as `Source::System` |

Both intake functions return `Error::HubNotSet` until a hub is installed.

## single_instance module

Available with the `single-instance` feature on Unix and Windows targets — full behavior in the [hand-off guide](/guides/single-instance/).

| Item | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `acquire` | `fn acquire(config: &Config, urls: &[String]) -> Result<Acquisition>` | After hub init: become primary or hand off to the running instance |
| `Acquisition::Primary(PrimaryGuard)` | enum variant | This process owns the socket; guard must live for the process lifetime |
| `Acquisition::HandedOff` | enum variant | `HandedOff { forwarded: usize }`; URLs delivered, caller should exit |
| `PrimaryGuard` | struct | Dropping closes the socket (and removes the Unix socket file) |

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Error reference" href="/reference/errors/" description="The shared Error type all these functions return." />
- <LinkCard title="Event sources explained" href="/explanation/event-sources/" description="System versus CommandLine semantics per platform." />


---

---
title: Build Your First Deep Link
description: Walk through creating a small Rust app that registers a custom URL scheme and receives deep-link events with nexum.
type: tutorial
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

In this tutorial you build a complete Rust program that owns the `myapp://` URL scheme. You register the scheme with your operating system, launch the app, open a `myapp://` URL from a terminal or browser, and watch the URL arrive inside your process. Along the way you meet the three pieces every nexum app uses: a `Config`, OS registration, and a `DeepLinkHandle`.

## Prerequisites

- Rust 1.85 or newer (nexum uses edition 2024). Check with `rustc --version`.
- A terminal on Windows, macOS or Linux.
- Roughly ten minutes.

## Step 1 — Create a project

Create a new binary crate and change into it:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo new nexum-demo
cd nexum-demo`} />

## Step 2 — Add the nexum facade

The `nexum` facade is the one-dependency path: it re-exports `Config`, the platform layer, and the `#[deep_link]` attribute.

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo add nexum`} />

Your `Cargo.toml` gains:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
nexum = "0.3"`} />

## Step 3 — Write the bootstrap

Replace the contents of `src/main.rs` with:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use nexum::deep_link;

#[deep_link(schemes = ["myapp"])]
fn main() {
    // Registration happens before this body runs; the consumer
    // handle is bound to \`_nexum_handle\`.
    if let Ok(url) = _nexum_handle.recv_blocking() {
                    println!("opened {url}");
    }
}`} />

The `#[deep_link]` attribute rewrites your `main` so that nexum builds a validated `Config` and calls `nexum::platform::init` *before* your first statement executes. The returned `DeepLinkHandle` is bound to the generated `_nexum_handle` binding, which you then use to receive URLs.

<Aside type="danger">
The generated code panics if the configuration is invalid or the OS registration fails. For fallible control — for example, to show an error dialog — use `nexum::platform::init` directly instead of the attribute.
</Aside>

## Step 4 — Run the app

Start the program and leave it running:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run`} />

On first run, nexum registers `myapp://` for your user:

- **Windows** — writes `HKCU\Software\Classes\myapp` with a `shell\open\command` entry pointing at the current executable.
- **macOS** — installs an Apple-event handler for the `GURL` event class. Packaged apps also need the scheme declared in `Info.plist`, which you can generate with `nexum::platform::plist::url_types_xml`.
- **Linux** — writes a `.desktop` file into your user applications directory and calls `xdg-mime default` to bind the scheme.

## Step 5 — Trigger the deep link

With the app still running, open a `myapp://` URL from another terminal:

<Code lang="bash" code={`# macOS
open "myapp://open/settings"

# Linux
xdg-open "myapp://open/settings"

# Windows (PowerShell)
Start-Process "myapp://open/settings"`} />

The operating system looks up the handler and launches — or, on Windows and Linux, re-launches — the registered executable with the URL. Nexum detects the URL among the process arguments and relays it into your app.

Where the output appears depends on your platform:

- **macOS** — the URL travels to the *running* instance as an Apple event, and the first app prints `opened myapp://open/settings`.
- **Windows and Linux** — the OS starts a *second* instance with the URL on its command line; that second process reaches the `println!` in its own terminal. To forward the URL into the original process and exit the second instance, enable the single-instance feature described in [Single-instance hand-off](/guides/single-instance/).

## What you built

You now have a Rust program that owns a URL scheme end to end: the OS launches it for `myapp://` URLs, nexum extracts the URL from the launch context, and `recv_blocking()` hands it to your code as a `String`.

<Aside type="tip">
Every event is a `DeepLinkEvent` with a `url` and a `source`. Call `recv_event_blocking()` instead of `recv_blocking()` to see where an event came from — runtime hand-offs and command-line cold starts are distinguishable via `Source`.
</Aside>

## Next steps

Adapt the same workflow to your UI framework of choice, or dive into the primitives:

- <LinkCard title="Platform setup guides" href="/guides/macos-setup/" description="Declare your scheme in Info.plist, the Windows registry or a .desktop file." />
- <LinkCard title="Core API reference" href="/reference/core/" description="Config, DeepLinkHub, DeepLinkHandle and DeepLinkEvent signatures." />
